sights.w: A free roadside sculpture garden of larger-than-life outsider art welded from old car and truck parts — a spider built from a whole VW Beetle, a bumblebee from a cement truck. One of northwest PA's most-photographed oddities; park in the gravel lot along Hershey Road.

A 587-acre undeveloped stretch of Lake Erie shoreline twelve miles west of the city, where trails run through oak savanna and along 90-foot bluffs to a wild, uncrowded beach and the mouth of Elk Creek — the quiet, rugged counterpart to Presque Isle.

sights.n: Splash Lagoon Indoor Water Park Resort
sights.w: A Polynesian-themed indoor water park kept at 84 degrees year-round — nine slides, a 30,000-square-foot wave pool, a FlowRider and a five-story treehouse — attached to several hotels off Peach Street. One of Erie's top family attractions, rain or snow.

A free 234-acre Millcreek nature preserve with five miles of trails, a boardwalk through a wooded wetland and a year-round nature center — a beloved local spot for birding, maple-sugaring programs and easy family walks.

sights.address: Soldiers & Sailors Home grounds, 560 E 3rd St, Erie, PA 16507
sights.w: An 1880 state-built replica of the Fort Presque Isle blockhouse marking where General 'Mad' Anthony Wayne died in 1796 — and the site of one of early America's strangest burials: his flesh was boiled from his bones in 1809 so the skeleton could be carried to eastern PA, and the boiled remains reburied here.

Housed in Erie's old Fire Station No. 4 (active 1903–1974), a two-floor collection of 1,500-plus artifacts — antique pumps, alarm systems, helmets and uniforms — tracing the history of American firefighting, run by retired Erie firefighters.

sights.address: North Pier, Presque Isle State Park, Erie, PA 16505
sights.w: The shortest of Erie's three lighthouses at 34 feet, standing at the tip of Presque Isle where the bay meets the lake — and the last square, pyramidal-style light tower left in the United States. A 20-minute drive from the park entrance and a favorite sunset perch.
